bull_bear.body: Net cash position INR 837cr; capex prioritized for BESS, steel plant, solar; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on debt-free growth and vertical integration
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Iron ore price volatility; BESS component cost inflation (lithium); delays in steel plant commissioning; export market access; regulatory delays in environmental clearances; global steel demand slowdown
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; transparent on CAPEX revisions; emphasizes decarbonization, export readiness, and vertical integration; acknowledges Q1 price softening but remains bullish on long-term demand
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: BESS margins are higher than initially modeled (12-13% vs 7-8%) due to Indian grid instability demand; EV fleet adoption cut diesel costs by 75% and emissions by 88%; pellet premium pricing will emerge post-monsoon (Q3) as high-grade output rises; INR 100cr CAPEX saved by switching from coal gasification to natural gas for pellets
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet framed as net cash: Net Cash (FY26) of Rs 837 Cr, with ROCE (FY26) of 17% and CFO up 29% FY26 vs FY25.
- CRISIL reaffirmed long-term and short-term credit ratings at AA-/Stable and A1+ respectively.
- Growth is being funded with measured leverage - CRM at Rs 550 Cr debt plus internal accruals, BESS at 1:1 debt-to-equity - against consolidated long-term borrowings of Rs 238 Cr and short-term of Rs 189 Cr at 31.03.2026.
- The company exited Ardent Steel entirely, reducing its stake from 37.85% to 0%, described as simplifying the group structure.
- Employee alignment via ESOPs: 50 lakh total options granted representing 2.22% of total paid-up equity capital, of which 31 lakh vested and 10 lakh exercised till 31-Mar-26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Pellets: 4.7Mn ton capacity (2Mn ton new plant commissioned Dec’25); Sponge iron: 0.65Mn ton capacity (up from 0.59Mn ton); Structural rolled: 3.75L tons FY27 target; BESS: 20GW project (Phase 1: 5-6GW FY28); Solar: 540MW total (165MW existing + 125MW by Jul’26); Mining: 4Mn ton ore mined FY26 (3.4Mn ton usable post-beneficiation)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as an integrated steel platform with captive iron ore mines and captive power generation, with end-to-end presence across the value chain from iron ore mining, pellets and sponge iron to finished steel products.
- Claims 100% captive iron ore security backed by two magnetite mines with 165 MnT proven reserves, 6.7 MnT capacity and 35+ years of mine life.
- Positioned as "25+ Years of Trust, Scale & Operating Discipline" across four pillars - Mining, Steel, Ferro Alloys and Energy.
- Group structure spans the Siltara integrated plant and Urla facilities in Chhattisgarh, two captive mines (Ari Dongri 6 mn MTPA, Boria Tibu 0.7 mn MTPA), and Godawari New Energy Pvt Ltd, a 100% subsidiary in Maharashtra for the BESS business.
- Industry context slide places GPIL inside a pellet market where JSW (28 MnT FY26P), AM/NS (14), Tata (13) and Jindal Steel (10) lead, with "Others" at 55 of the 120 MnT total.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Vision 2030] Backed by a strong balance sheet and captive mining assets, the deck targets approximately 4x revenue (Rs 5,381 Cr in FY26 to Rs 24,000 Cr in 2030E), ~3x EBITDA (Rs 1,253 Cr to Rs 3,500 Cr) and ~3x PAT (Rs 802 Cr to Rs 2,500 Cr).
- [Macro headwind] Sequential profitability was hit by elevated coal prices and increased market sourcing of iron ore following the West Asia crisis - a named external shock, not an operating deterioration.
- [State incentives] The Maharashtra Government approved multiple incentives for the BESS project including electricity duty and stamp duty exemptions, power tariff subsidy, interest and capital subsidies, SGST-linked incentives and ESI/EPF reimbursements.
- [Shareholding] Promoter and Promoter Group hold 63.18% as on 30-Jun-26, with FPI at 6.00%, domestic institutions 3.10% and non-institution 27.72% of 67,30,97,430 total shares.
- [Workforce] Attrition of 4.6%, average employee age 42 years and average tenure 10 years; term insurance for 100% of employees, group medical cover for 91%; Great Place to Work certified.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Pellet margin: INR 2,000/ton conversion cost; DRI: 40% iron ore, 35% coal, 25% opex; BESS margin: 12-13% currently (conservative 7-8% assumed); mining cost: INR 3,000-3,200/ton; freight saving: INR 150/ton post-beneficiation at mine
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: >INR 6,000cr in FY27; margin: 24-25% EBITDA margin; order inflow: 20GW BESS (commissioning Mar’27), 1Mn ton steel plant (construction Oct’26); capex/commissioning: 540MW solar (55MW commissioned, 100MW by Jul’26), 2Mn ton pellet plant (Dec’25), CRM (Mar’27), BESS (Mar’27), Ari Dongri mine expansion (FY28)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 6 months for structural rolled products; long-term BESS supply agreements signed with EVE and Roche; no explicit order book for steel plant yet
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 20GW BESS (INR 15,000cr revenue potential); 1Mn ton integrated steel plant (INR 6,000cr revenue potential); CRM (INR 3,000-4,000cr revenue); Boria Tibu mine expansion to 4Mn ton (FY30); potential new mine auctions
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q4 FY26 performance driven by pellet and rolled product ramp-up, with EBITDA margin holding at 23% despite softer realizations; key catalysts are the 20GW BESS, 1Mn ton integrated steel plant, and 540MW solar expansion, positioning GPIL as a vertically integrated low-carbon steel and energy transition player.

open.item: Q2 landed imported coal cost about INR11,000 (RB1, 6000 GCV); Q3 expected between INR10,500-11,000 (dollar rise offsetting index fall).
Expect roughly 5% to 7% additional volume/top line in FY26 from new pellet plant and new structural rolling mill (additional ~1 lakh tons).
New gas-based pellet plant makes company export-ready; may start exporting pellets from next quarter if domestic demand stays weak (export delta now less than $10).

War-driven sea freight and dollar rise to lift imported coal price by 15-20% from Q2 FY27; mining transportation cost up Rs.200-250, could reach Rs.1,150-1,200 per ton; can switch to abundant domestic coal.
Iron ore beneficiation plant capacity expansion at Ari Dongri (10-fold to 6 million tons) targeted for commissioning by Q3 FY27.

0.7 million ton CRM complex on-site construction to commission by July FY26; key equipment orders placed with advances released; project targeted for commissioning by March FY27; 50% utilization FY28, 90% FY29.
FY27 capex about Rs.1,500-2,000 crores (balance CRM, BESS, solar, steel advances ~10%); FY28 and FY29 ~Rs.3,000 crores each (mainly steel plant), debt raised from FY28.
FY27 top line should cross Rs.6,000 crores with new pellet plant at 80-90% capacity; EBITDA margin ~24-25% at current market levels.

BESS project scaled to 20 GW (Phase-1); long-term agreements signed with EVE Power (628 Ah LFP cells) and Shanghai Shenyi Roche (balance of system); commissioning from March '27; first year 5-6 GW output.
FY27 pellet production guidance of 4 million tons; captive ~0.9-1 million tons, merchant ~3 million tons.
FY27 net usable iron ore guidance of 3.4 million tons (actual mining ~4-4.5 million tons including Boria Tibu); ~0.8-1 million tons iron ore procurement this year, dropping post-Diwali.
Expect CRM conversion margin of about 7-8% average (up to 10%) buying HRC from market on long-term basis.
Target long-term EBITDA of Rs. 10,000 per ton on the proposed integrated steel plant on a conservative long-term average basis.
BESS Phase-1 (20 GW line): first year FY28 5-6 GW output (~30-40%), second year 12-14 GW (~70%), third year 17-18 GW (~90%); margin ~7-8% conservative (currently 12-13%).

Received EC and consent to operate for Ari Dongri expansion 2.35 to 6 million tons in February '26; phased ramp-up begun, rated 6 million ton capacity targeted end Q3/early Q4 FY27, full scale from FY28.
Generating about Rs.800-1,000 crores free cash every year; expect minimum Rs.3,000 crores free cash in FY27/FY28 post mining approval and new pellet plant.
Plan to expand Boria Tibu mining from 0.7 to 4 million tons with in-mine beneficiation; online by ~FY30, usable output ~1.5 million tons; timed with new steel plant.

2031 vision: top line from announced projects (BESS ~Rs.15,000cr at 16 GW, steel plant ~Rs.6,000cr, CRM ~Rs.3,000-4,000cr, plus pellet) with ~Rs.3,000 crore PAT at ~10% PAT margin; margins diluted by low-margin BESS/CRM.
Plan to shift existing transport fleet to EV (~300-350 trucks) at full-scale CAPEX of about Rs.350 crores to cut diesel cost; EV vehicles already reduced operating costs ~75% and emissions ~88%.
Expect steel plant EBITDA of more than 20% once operating at full capacity (value-added structural steel, limited competition).
